title: Latency rows per endpoint, with a wrong claim in a thread

pr.title: Add latency rows for the on-call dashboard
pr.description: Adds `latencyRows()`, which gives the average response time of each endpoint over the last five minutes and marks an endpoint over 800 ms as slow. `pages()` pages on-call for each slow row.

bugs.note: averageMs() divides by zero when the window has no sample with a response time. collect() returns an empty list for an endpoint without traffic (collect.ts), so the average is NaN, the status is slow, and pages() pages on-call for an idle endpoint. The thread claim that collect() never returns an empty list is wrong.

traps.why: == null is on purpose and correct: it skips a sample whose ms is null. A finding that asks for === is no defect.

threads.author: reviewer-1
threads.text: Which samples does averageMs() get from collect() for each endpoint?

threads.author: eval-author
threads.text: This case is handled: collect() never returns an empty list. For an idle endpoint it returns the last sample before the window, so count is at least 1.
